It checks WholeScaling(1,1,1,2), Valid, Nested, homoskedasticity, zero target, and scaled true variance one, and proves that its product law is exactly wholeFairSignLaw. Its final T34 data example includes every witness-data clause, without invoking a Challenge theorem. Analytically, n*printedAuxiliary=1-betaHat^2 on the support, and E[betaHat^2]=1/n, so Markov's inequality gives the claimed less-than-epsilon probability limit one for every epsilon>0 and every coefficient array; it cannot also tend to zero. Set theta_i=1 and D_i=(1,delta_i), with delta=(1,-2,1) in each triple; the true coefficient is (0,1), D^T D=diag(n,2n), and the first scaled OLS row is identically one. Then beta=0, Var(U_i)=29/15, |Y_i|<=4<=6, true degrees<=2, |theta_i|<2, and n Var(betaHat)=29/15; the full and observed path graphs nest. Independent bounded block averages give n V1(G,Y) ->p 19/15, so the underestimation probability for epsilon=1/3 tends to one. scratch/Nonvacuity.lean compiles the exact three-row Gram, invertibility, mean-model matrix identity, OLS-weight, and negative mean-quadratic identities. scratch/Counterexamples.py checks exact noise/block moments and enumerates the first two full rows. The entire asymptotic existential is justified here analytically, not re-proved by the scratch Lean file.

It proves the full disjoint-set random-vector dependency condition, the a.e. coordinate bound, positive growing sizes, zero target, variance n/n^2, and scaled variance exactly one.
